title: A treatment that changes the course of schizophrenia

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a treatment that produces a substantial, lasting improvement in cognition and everyday functioning for people with schizophrenia, with benefits that persist after the investigational intervention ends. It would change the illness’s clinical trajectory beyond reducing symptoms during an acute episode. The capability remains a goal in the supplied evidence; it has not been demonstrated by the studies summarized here.

Conceptual synthesis: PSY-02 is defined by the clinical outcome rather than by a particular biological mechanism or treatment format. A medicine, rehabilitation intervention, or combined approach could qualify if it met convincing causal, magnitude, and durability criteria. Demonstrating this outcome would establish a change in clinical course; establishing biological repair would require additional evidence.

significance.text: Antipsychotics can reduce the positive symptoms of schizophrenia, including acute psychosis, but their efficacy for cognitive and negative symptoms is limited. These remaining difficulties can obstruct everyday recovery even when acute symptoms improve. A treatment that substantially improved both cognition and functioning would address a major gap between symptom control and sustained recovery.

Conditional synthesis: replicated, clinically large gains that persist after treatment ends would show that an intervention can durably alter schizophrenia’s clinical course in the population demonstrated to benefit. Depending on the functional outcomes actually measured, downstream possibilities could include greater independence and participation in relationships, education, or employment. Those consequences would require direct measurement rather than inference from cognitive test scores alone.

Schizophrenia does not inevitably deteriorate: the long-term prognosis review explicitly recognizes that recovery is possible. Consequently, a persuasive advance must show an advantage over an appropriate comparison, rather than attribute every recovery to the intervention. Even a successful trial would not establish universal recovery, prevention of schizophrenia, or transfer of the treatment to other psychiatric disorders.

missing_breakthrough.text: The missing capability is a reproducible intervention that produces a clinically substantial and sustained improvement in both cognition and everyday function. The evidence identifies unmet cognitive and negative-symptom needs, but it does not establish a single biological process responsible for continuing disability or prove that every approved treatment lacks long-term benefits. The failure of one phase 3 cognitive-treatment programme narrows the evidence for that intervention; it does not show that cognitive recovery is impossible.

Scientific and engineering synthesis: candidate interventions must bridge several distinct gaps—producing a meaningful cognitive benefit, translating that benefit into daily functioning, and maintaining it after the intervention stops. A new receptor target or a short-term symptom response does not itself establish any of these capabilities. Conversely, a clinically successful intervention could establish course change before its complete biological mechanism was understood.

Demonstration-design synthesis: the central measurement barriers are separating treatment effects from recovery that would otherwise occur, distinguishing cognitive test improvement from meaningful functional recovery, and estimating persistence without selecting only people who successfully discontinue treatment. Long follow-up must also establish safety and tolerability. The five-week xanomeline–trospium trial itself identifies its short duration as a limitation for assessing durability and long-term safety.

current_state.text: A 2022 systematic review and meta-analysis included 14 prospective studies comprising 1,991 patients, published between 1978 and 2020, with at least 20 years of follow-up. It estimated recovery at 24.2 percent using a harmonized assessment template and described limited historical change in prognosis, while emphasizing that recovery is possible. The supplied review assessed the abstract-level evidence, which does not provide a complete account of individual cohorts or treatment histories.

The supplied research attributes a median recovery rate of 13.5 percent to an earlier synthesis, published online in November 2012, using both clinical and social recovery sustained for two years. It also attributes a lack of improvement across decades to that synthesis. These details remain unverified within the supplied review because the source text was not captured. That access limitation does not establish that the figures are false. The 13.5 percent and 24.2 percent estimates should not be read as a direct historical trend: the syntheses differ in recovery definitions and follow-up requirements.

On 26 September 2024, the FDA approved xanomeline–trospium, marketed as Cobenfy, describing it as the first approved antipsychotic targeting cholinergic receptors rather than dopamine receptors. The approval evidence included two five-week randomized trials measuring change in total Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale scores. The 2024 EMERGENT-3 report studied people experiencing acute psychosis, recruited in inpatient settings, and reported a week-five PANSS difference of −8.4 points versus placebo. This established acute symptom efficacy, not durable cognitive and functional recovery. The supplied review had the main article text but not linked supplements or figure images.

The CONNEX programme report, published in the December 2025 issue of The Lancet Psychiatry, described three phase 3 trials of iclepertin for cognitive impairment associated with schizophrenia. Among 1,835 treated adults, iclepertin did not significantly outperform placebo on the MATRICS Consensus Cognitive Battery composite endpoint at 26 weeks: the adjusted difference was 0.127, with a confidence interval spanning zero and p=0.63. Its background described the absence of available pharmacotherapies for this cognitive impairment at publication. The supplied review assessed abstract-level evidence; it does not establish that CONNEX was the largest or leading programme across the field.

A review published in May 2026 surveyed negative-symptom treatment trials published from January 2024 through October 2025. Its abstract described generally modest effects and mostly small, methodologically heterogeneous randomized trials, with negative symptoms remaining an unmet treatment need. This is a bounded assessment of that publication period, not a survey of all developments through November 2026. The supplied evidence was limited to the formal abstract; a separate machine-generated summary was not used.

A June 2024 meta-analysis of cognitive remediation found statistically significant benefits persisting to the assessed follow-ups: standardized effects were d=0.23 for global cognition and d=0.26 for global functioning. These are demonstrated durable gains. The abstract-level evidence supplied does not establish a common two-year endpoint, persistence after a planned withdrawal, or attainment of the proposed large recovery threshold. It therefore neither demonstrates PSY-02 as defined here nor justifies categorically excluding rehabilitation from a future course-changing treatment.

Evidence boundary: these are dated findings assembled from the supplied research and review. No freshness-search record was provided to establish whether subsequent developments changed the treatment landscape by 1 November 2026. The record therefore supports the documented unmet goal and specific study results, rather than an exhaustive present-day claim about every available treatment.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: conduct a randomized trial in a clearly defined population with early or established schizophrenia, comparing the intervention with appropriate standard antipsychotic care. Use blinding where feasible and blinded outcome assessment, with pre-registered cognitive and everyday functional primary outcomes. Before enrollment, specify what counts as a clinically large benefit, any recovery thresholds, and how multiple outcomes will be analyzed. These are proposed requirements for this record, not established consensus standards.
completion_criteria.label: Randomized schizophrenia trial preregisters cognitive and everyday functional primary outcomes

completion_criteria.text: Proposed durability test: demonstrate that the advantage remains at two years and prospectively test persistence after the investigational intervention ends. A planned randomized withdrawal design, or another justified causal comparison, should retain appropriate standard care. Observing a selected subgroup who discontinue treatment would be insufficient on its own, because their outcomes may reflect selection rather than a lasting treatment effect. The proposed two-year duration is a demanding benchmark, not a source-defined threshold.
completion_criteria.label: Causal comparison demonstrates two-year benefits persisting after intervention ends

completion_criteria.text: Proposed confirmation: require independent replication, adequate retention, explicit handling of missing outcomes, and an acceptable long-term safety and tolerability profile. Report the illness stages, patient characteristics, care settings, and duration for which benefit is demonstrated. Successful finite trials would establish breadth within those boundaries, not literal universality or lifelong benefit.
completion_criteria.label: Independent replication confirms benefit with acceptable long-term safety and tolerability

completion_criteria.text: A five-week reduction in PANSS during acute psychosis would not satisfy these criteria because it does not measure the required long-term cognitive and functional outcomes. Durable cognitive-remediation effects provide relevant evidence that these outcomes can improve, but the reported average effects and follow-up information do not by themselves establish the proposed completion threshold.
completion_criteria.label: Acute PANSS reductions cannot establish durable cognitive and functional benefit

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: PSY-01, “Mechanism-defined diseases in place of the major syndromes,” concerns how psychiatric diseases are identified and explained. PSY-02 concerns a durable treatment outcome in schizophrenia. A mechanistic reclassification could help identify responsive populations, but clinical course change would not by itself replace syndromic diagnosis. PSY-05, “Medicines designed from a confirmed human disease mechanism,” concerns a treatment-design route; a medicine could satisfy both entries, while success on either criterion would not automatically satisfy the other.

Roster-based synthesis: PSY-04, “Primary prevention that lowers incidence of a major disorder,” concerns preventing new cases, whereas PSY-02 concerns improving the course of existing schizophrenia. PSY-10, “Reopening plasticity that can repair an established psychiatric deficit,” proposes one possible route to repair. A plasticity-based intervention could satisfy both PSY-10 and PSY-02 if it demonstrated the respective mechanism and clinical outcome, but durable recovery alone would not prove that plasticity had been reopened.

Roster-based synthesis: PSY-03, “Ending the relapsing course of severe mood disorders,” and PSY-09, “A time-limited reset of severe addiction,” share an interest in durable changes in illness trajectory. They retain separate identities because they concern different disorders and endpoints. PSY-12, “A session-level amplifier that lets brief psychotherapy match a full course,” concerns treatment efficiency; matching an existing course would not automatically establish the magnitude and persistence of recovery proposed for PSY-02.

Roster-based synthesis: PSY-06, “A clinical instrument that reads an individual’s psychiatric state,” could support measurement or treatment selection but is an assessment capability. PSY-07, “Reliable causal control of a core symptom by a defined circuit,” could contribute a therapeutic mechanism, but controlling one symptom would not by itself establish broad cognitive and functional recovery. PSY-08, “Selective and durable modification of a pathological memory,” and PSY-11, “Prevention of post-traumatic stress disorder by blocking consolidation,” concern distinct memory targets and, for PSY-11, prevention. Their success would require separate evidence before being extended to schizophrenia’s course.

brief.title: Lasting recovery from schizophrenia
possible: People with schizophrenia could gain lasting improvements in thinking and everyday life that continue after a treatment ends. The treatment could be a medicine, rehabilitation, or a combination.
Those gains could help people live more independently and participate in relationships, education or work.
why: Medicines can ease psychosis, including hallucinations, while difficulties with thinking and motivation continue to obstruct daily life. Improving both thinking and everyday functioning would close a major gap between symptom relief and sustained recovery.

sources.showed: Their review of long-term studies estimated that 24.2% of people had recovered. Schizophrenia does not inevitably worsen.
sources.cited_for: Recovery is possible, so a treatment must demonstrate an advantage over an appropriate comparison.
sources.not_established: The review does not establish that a particular treatment caused lasting recovery.

sources.who: Authors of the earlier recovery review
sources.showed: This review combined studies of sustained clinical and social recovery in schizophrenia.
sources.cited_for: It provides background on sustained recovery in schizophrenia.
sources.not_established: Recovery estimates alone do not demonstrate that a treatment changes the illness's course.

sources.showed: The FDA approved Cobenfy after trials showed symptom relief over five weeks.
sources.quote: In both studies, the participants who received Cobenfy experienced a meaningful reduction in symptoms from baseline to Week 5 as measured by the PANSS Total Score compared to the placebo group.
sources.not_established: The approval trials did not establish lasting improvements in thinking and everyday functioning after treatment ends.

sources.showed: Xanomeline–trospium, marketed as Cobenfy, reduced symptoms more than a placebo, a dummy treatment, during acute psychosis.
sources.quote: Xanomeline-trospium was efficacious and well tolerated in people with schizophrenia experiencing acute psychosis.
sources.cited_for: Short-term relief of psychosis is an established treatment outcome.
sources.not_established: The trial did not demonstrate durable cognitive and everyday functional recovery.

sources.who: Richard S E Keefe and colleagues
sources.showed: Their trials found that iclepertin did not significantly improve thinking test scores compared with a dummy treatment after 26 weeks.
sources.cited_for: A medicine specifically tested for thinking difficulties failed to demonstrate benefit.
sources.not_established: This failure does not establish that lasting cognitive recovery is impossible.

sources.who: Louise Birkedal Glenthøj, Mette Ødegaard Nielsen and Merete Nordentoft
sources.showed: Their review found generally modest treatment effects on negative symptoms, such as reduced motivation. Most trials were small and varied in design.
sources.quote: Most recent RCTs were small and methodologically heterogeneous, and effects on negative symptoms were generally modest.
sources.cited_for: Reduced motivation and related difficulties remain an unmet treatment need.
sources.not_established: The reviewed trials did not establish substantial, lasting recovery in thinking and daily functioning.

sources.showed: Their combined analysis found modest benefits from cognitive remediation, rehabilitation aimed at improving thinking skills. Gains in thinking and functioning persisted at follow-up.
sources.quote: Cognitive remediation provides durable improvements in cognition and functioning in schizophrenia.
sources.cited_for: Rehabilitation can produce lasting improvements in both thinking and functioning.
sources.not_established: The findings do not establish large benefits maintained after a planned treatment withdrawal at a shared long-term endpoint.

shown: Antonio Vita and colleagues found that rehabilitation aimed at thinking skills produced modest gains in thinking and everyday functioning that persisted at follow-up. This demonstrates lasting improvement in the outcomes that matter.

Inder Kaul and colleagues showed that Cobenfy relieved acute psychosis. Richard S E Keefe and colleagues found no significant thinking benefit from iclepertin. Neither result demonstrates substantial recovery that continues after treatment ends.
missing: A treatment has yet to demonstrate substantial gains in both thinking and everyday functioning that meet the proposed recovery threshold.
A fair comparison has yet to establish that those gains persist after the treatment ends.
Independent teams have yet to reproduce that full result with acceptable long-term safety and tolerability.

milestones.label: A randomized trial commits to thinking and daily-life outcomes
milestones.explanation: A trial with randomly assigned treatment groups would have to publish its thinking and daily-functioning outcomes and success thresholds before enrollment. This makes the test of meaningful recovery explicit.

milestones.label: Benefits last two years and survive treatment ending
milestones.explanation: A fair comparison would have to show benefits lasting two years and persisting after the treatment ends, while standard care continues. This separates a lasting treatment effect from recovery that would otherwise occur.

milestones.label: Independent studies confirm benefit and acceptable long-term safety
milestones.explanation: Independent teams would have to reproduce the benefit, account for missing outcomes and establish acceptable long-term safety and tolerability. This would establish reliability and identify who benefits.

milestones.label: Short-term symptom relief falls short of lasting recovery
milestones.explanation: A five-week drop in symptom scores would not establish durable gains in thinking and everyday functioning. Existing lasting rehabilitation benefits also fall short of demonstrating the proposed large recovery threshold.

uncertain: How large must improvements in thinking and everyday life be to count as a meaningful change in the illness's course?
When should treatment end, and how should lasting benefit be tested? The proposed two-year benchmark is not an established standard.
Which people and treatment approaches could achieve lasting recovery, and what safety tradeoffs would be acceptable?

page.title: Sustained cognitive and functional recovery in schizophrenia
page.definition: A treatment improves cognition—memory, attention and reasoning—and increases sustained symptomatic and functional recovery in schizophrenia. Both advantages persist for two years after the investigational intervention ends, while indicated background care continues.

goal.need: A 2022 review included 14 cohorts comprising 1,991 participants with follow-up of at least 20 years; its pooled recovery estimate was 24.2% (95% CI 20.3–28.0%) under harmonized outcome definitions. A 2024 meta-analysis of 67 randomized cognitive-remediation studies comprising 5,334 participants found follow-up benefits in cognition and functioning. The goal is to increase sustained cognitive and functional recovery beyond these observed outcomes.

figures.caption: Cognitive remediation effects at the end of follow-up in the 2024 meta-analysis
figures.note: Cohen's d expresses the treatment–control difference in standard-deviation units. Follow-up durations varied.

statements.quote: CNTRICS endeavors to translate the tools and insights from cognitive neuroscience into better treatments for schizophrenia
statements.context: CNTRICS is the Cognitive Neuroscience Approaches to the Treatment of Impaired Cognition in Schizophrenia initiative.

statements.body: International Society for CNS Clinical Trials and Methodology (ISCTM) consensus panel
statements.quote: Cognitive impairment and functional disability were viewed as equally important treatment targets.
statements.context: The consensus meeting took place on 20 March 2014; its report was published online on 11 September 2015.

statements.quote: further research is needed to develop specific treatments for cognitive impairment in schizophrenia.

completion.title: Randomized trials show cognitive and recovery benefits lasting two years after treatment ends.
completion.criterion: Two independently conducted randomized controlled studies in people with schizophrenia show superiority over a control receiving the same indicated background care in both a validated cognitive composite and the proportion meeting Liberman et al.'s recovery criteria. Both advantages persist for two consecutive years after the scheduled end of the investigational intervention. The recovery criteria are specified in m4; statistical tests for both outcomes control multiplicity.
completion.set_by: Atlas operational test; no external body located defines this combined post-treatment endpoint.
completion.basis: Searches covered EMA schizophrenia guidance, NIMH trial guidance, ISCTM disease-modification discussions and published recovery definitions. None supplies a joint post-cessation cognitive-and-recovery test. The two-year recovery convention supplies the functional threshold; applying it after cessation and requiring independent randomized confirmation are Atlas choices. This tests clinical course change without asserting biological repair.

milestones.title: A candidate schizophrenia treatment engages its proposed target in humans at a tolerated dose.
milestones.criterion: An intervention changes its hypothesised molecular, circuit, cognitive or behavioural target in humans, meeting the study-specific target-engagement criterion at a tolerated dose. NIMH sets no universal percentage cutoff. Rosenbrock et al. (2018) found that iclepertin raised cerebrospinal-fluid glycine by 61% versus vehicle in rats (0.6 mg/kg; eight/group), and by 57% from baseline before the final dose of a 14-day, 10 mg/day regimen in healthy men (four evaluable men; 25 men across doses). These are indirect measures of brain glycine-transporter inhibition.
milestones.set_by: NIMH experimental-therapeutics clinical-trial programme; this is an early human development gate across intervention modalities.
milestones.threshold_quote: If the intervention adequately engages the target/mechanism, one can then test whether the changes produced in the target/mechanism affect clinical outcomes.

milestones.title: A schizophrenia treatment improves the MCCB cognitive composite versus placebo at 12 weeks.
milestones.criterion: A blinded randomized study in clinically stable schizophrenia improves the MATRICS Consensus Cognitive Battery (MCCB) overall composite T-score at week 12. The iclepertin protocol tests a non-flat dose response across six models, controlling multiplicity at one-sided α=0.05. Between 25 April 2018 and 4 October 2019, 509 participants were randomized; five models passed. The 10 mg/day contrast was 1.98 T-score points (95% CI 0.43–3.53), reported in 2021.
milestones.set_by: Boehringer Ingelheim, protocol 1346.9, NCT02832037/EudraCT 2016-000285-28; this 12-week endpoint was set specifically for iclepertin.
milestones.threshold_quote: overall composite t-score after 12 weeks of treatment

milestones.title: A treatment sustains cognitive benefit for 6–12 months and preserves or improves functioning.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate cognitive-battery efficacy during at least six months on a stable dose and maintenance of cognitive benefit in a 6–12-month study, with clinically relevant functioning preserved or improved at the long-term endpoint. EMA accepts the MCCB or a comparably validated battery. CONNEX did not establish cognitive efficacy at 26 weeks: across three phase 3 trials, 1,835 adults received treatment; the iclepertin–placebo difference was 0.127 T-score points (95% CI −0.396 to 0.650; p=0.63), reported in 2025.
milestones.set_by: European Medicines Agency, CHMP schizophrenia guideline, section 4.5.2 (2012); the guidance concerns medicinal products.
milestones.threshold_quote: For this purpose, a maintenance of effect study of at least 6-12 months would suffice.

milestones.title: People with schizophrenia meet symptomatic and functional recovery criteria for two consecutive years.
milestones.criterion: For two consecutive years, meet Liberman et al.'s criteria: Brief Psychiatric Rating Scale positive and negative symptom items ≤4 (moderate); at least half-time competitive employment or schooling, with retirement alternatives; independent daily living without supervision; at least weekly contact with a non-family peer; and culturally appropriate cordial family relationships. Maintenance medication is permitted. The 2002 observational pilot identified 17 people with schizophrenia and six with schizoaffective disorder meeting the definition; it did not establish a treatment effect.
milestones.set_by: Liberman, Kopelowicz, Ventura and Gutkind, operational recovery definition (2002), Table 1 and accompanying text; a published research convention rather than a regulatory standard.
milestones.threshold_quote: each of the above criteria should be sustained for at least two consecutive years.

not_found: No external standard was located that specifies both a minimum cognitive benefit and its required duration after intervention cessation in schizophrenia.
No controlled result located demonstrated the complete post-cessation cognitive-and-recovery test.
The full text of the supplied May 2026 review of negative-symptom treatment trials could not be opened.

results.finding: In long-term schizophrenia follow-up studies, 24.2% were classified as recovered (n = 246).
results.detail: The meta-analysis used a unified outcome template across studies with differing definitions. The text does not establish that participants met Liberman et al.’s criteria for two consecutive years.
results.quote: Our meta-analysis found that 24.2 % had 'recovered' (n = 246, CI: 20.3-28.0 %), 35.5 % had a 'good or better' outcome (n = 766, CI: 26.0-45.0%), and 59.7% had 'moderate or better' outcome (n = 1139, CI: 49.3-70.1 %).

results.finding: In 1,835 patients, iclepertin’s week-26 MCCB advantage over placebo was 0.127 T-score points.
results.detail: The difference was not statistically significant (95% CI −0.396 to 0.650; p=0.63). The excerpt does not report a long-term functioning outcome.
results.quote: The adjusted mean difference for iclepertin versus placebo for MCCB overall composite T-score was 0·127 [95% CI -0·396 to 0·650]; p=0·63).

results.finding: A meta-analysis of 67 studies with 5,334 participants found a global cognition effect of d=0.23 at follow-up.
results.detail: Global functioning also improved at follow-up (d=0.26). The text does not establish at least six months of treatment or a 6–12-month endpoint.
results.quote: Cognitive remediation produced statistically significant positive effects that persisted at the end of follow-up in global cognition (d=0.23) and in global functioning (d=0.26).

results.finding: In schizophrenia, BI 425809 improved the week-12 MCCB composite versus placebo by 1.982 T-score points at 10 mg/day; 509 participants were randomized.
results.detail: The double-blind trial enrolled patients on stable antipsychotic treatment. Five of six prespecified dose-response models passed multiplicity-adjusted testing. The 10 mg contrast was a secondary analysis with a nominal p-value; its 95% CI was 0.434–3.53.

results.finding: Among 145 outpatients, NET plus work therapy produced more hours worked than work therapy alone (p < 0.03).
results.detail: The study reports improved work outcomes, with differences emerging after rehabilitation. The provided text does not report cognitive-battery efficacy during treatment or maintained cognitive benefit at follow-up.
results.quote: NET+WT worked more hours than WT (p < 0.03), with differences emerging after rehabilitation.

results.finding: In 60 patients with first-episode schizophrenia, cognitive remediation improved cognition in the injectable risperidone group and improved work/school functioning.
results.detail: The trial lasted 12 months, but the text does not identify the cognitive battery, establish a stable medication dose, or specify whether cognitive benefit and functioning were maintained at the long-term endpoint.
results.quote: Cognitive remediation was superior to healthy behavior training in the LAI medication condition but not the oral medication condition.
